question.text: Will November 2026 be the warmest November on record, according to Copernicus?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if November 2026 is the warmest November on record (when evaluated by global average air surface temperature for the month) in the ERA5 [dataset](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels?tab=overview), according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S)--for example in its monthly [Climate Bulletin](https://climate.copernicus.eu/climate-bulletin).

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-30: I did not fetch the ERA5 dataset or the C3S bulletin page directly. The current record to beat, from C3S, is November 2023: 14.22°C, which is +0.85°C above the 1991-2020 average and about 1.75°C above pre-industrial. [C3S Nov 2023](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2023)
- 2025-12-10: November 2025 came in third at 14.02°C (+0.65°C), 0.20°C below 2023 and 0.08°C below November 2024 (second). [C3S Nov 2025](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2025)
- C3S should publish the November 2026 bulletin in early December, after the question's nominal resolution time of 2026-12-01.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled this yet. November has not started.
- 2026-10-30: celsius.earth is a third-party tracker, not Copernicus. Using ERA5 daily data through 2026-10-29, it estimates October 2026 at 15.364°C, or +0.92°C vs 1991-2020 (+1.80°C vs pre-industrial). That would be the warmest October, about 0.07°C above October 2023. [celsius.earth](https://celsius.earth/warmest-month)
- The same page forecasts November 2026 at 14.20°C, an anomaly of +0.83°C (90% range +0.66 to +1.01). That is just under the +0.85°C record. It gives the record a 42% chance in its "standard" run and 59% when "re-seeded". The same site's figures have been inconsistent before: a search snippet showed a 45% chance for October, but the current page says 100%.
- Key point: October's anomaly (~+0.92) sits well above the November bar (+0.85), and El Niño is still strengthening. If November simply held October's anomaly, it would set a record.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-30: Business Today, citing an ECMWF ensemble via Netweather, reports an 86% chance of a major sudden stratospheric warming in early November, linked to the "Super El Niño". This could redistribute cold air in the Northern Hemisphere. The effect on the global mean is unclear. [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/world/story/arctic-polar-vortex-could-weaken-like-never-before-in-november-what-super-el-nino-has-to-do-with-it-564701-2026-10-30)
- 2026-10-28/29: Forecasters expect an omega block over Europe and possible cold air from the east in early November. These are regional signals only. [Futura](https://www.futura-sciences.com/planete/actualites/meteo-meteo-va-bloquer-france-pendant-10-15-jours-voici-cest-mauvaise-nouvelle-138904/), [Il Mattino](https://www.ilmattino.it/primopiano/cronaca/meteo_inverno_2026_2027_freddo_novembre_neve-9856429.html)
- 2026-10 (September bulletin): C3S reported September 2026 as the second warmest September, at 16.27°C (+0.82°C, 1.63°C above pre-industrial), 0.11°C below 2023. Extra-polar sea surface temperature hit a September record of 21.05°C. Niño 3.4 set an all-time high for the month, above the 2015/16 peaks. C3S Director Buontempo said the run of months above 1.5°C will likely last into 2027. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/global-temperatures-remain-over-15degc-above-pre-industrial-levels-during-second-warmest-september), [sustainabilityonline](https://sustainabilityonline.net/news/september-2026-was-the-second-warmest-on-record-says-copernicus/)
- 2026-09: C3S reported August 2026 as the joint warmest month on record. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/copernicus-august-was-worlds-joint-hottest-month-record-pushing-global-temperatures-back-above)

## 4. Base rates
- ERA5 November anomalies vs 1991-2020: 2023 was +0.85 (record), 2024 about +0.73, 2025 +0.65. The previous record before 2023, November 2020, was 0.32°C lower than 2023. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2023)
- Recent 2026 anomalies: September +0.82 (2023 was +0.93), October about +0.92 (estimated). The anomaly rose roughly 0.1°C from September to October.
- Analog: in the 2023 El Niño build-up, every month from June to December set a calendar-month record. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2023) The bar for November is relatively high, because 2023's November anomaly (+0.85) was only a little below its September and October values.
- Persistence: month-to-month changes in the global anomaly are typically about ±0.05 to 0.1°C. During a strengthening El Niño, global temperatures usually lag Niño 3.4 by a few months, which points to further warming into winter.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "This November is the hottest November ever?": Yes at 0.76 (2026-10-30 13:27 UTC). I could not confirm its resolution source; it may be NASA or NOAA rather than C3S.
- Kalshi, "November temperature increase": the 1.30+ bucket is at 0.53 and all lower buckets at about 0. This is probably the NASA GISS anomaly scale, so it only maps to this question indirectly.
- Polymarket: October 2026 as hottest October at 0.968. 2026 ranked #1 year at 0.895.
- Kalshi: 2026 hottest year at 0.80.
- celsius.earth model: 42% to 59% chance of a November record. [celsius.earth](https://celsius.earth/warmest-month)
- Manifold: there is an October 2026 ranking market, but I found no November market. I found no official C3S or ECMWF statement forecasting November specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-11-05 to 11-08: the C3S October 2026 bulletin is due. It should confirm whether October set a record and by how much, which tests the persistence argument.
- Daily ERA5 values on Climate Pulse (pulse.climate.copernicus.eu) through November will give a running month-to-date picture.
- Early to mid November: the possible sudden stratospheric warming, along with the NOAA and BoM El Niño updates (CPC update around 2026-11-12).
- About 2026-12-04 to 12-09: the C3S November bulletin, the actual resolution document.

**Summary:** October 2026 is running about 0.07°C above the previous October record, with El Niño still strengthening. November needs to reach +0.85°C or more vs 1991-2020. One model's central estimate is just below that at +0.83, but simple persistence from October would clear it.

Current forecasts put November 2026 roughly level with the record, so this looks close to a coin flip. One independent ERA5-based model gives it a 42% chance of a record, while Kalshi prices it at 76%. Nothing has settled it yet, because November has not started.

## 1. Resolution source
- **Record to beat:** The resolving dataset is C3S ERA5 global surface air temperature, reported in the monthly Climate Bulletin. The current November record is November 2023. It is not listed directly in a source I fetched, but working back from C3S's 2025 bulletin it is about +0.85°C above the 1991-2020 average, roughly 14.22°C. [C3S Nov 2025](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2025)
- **2025-12-09/10:** November 2025 was third warmest, at 14.02°C (+0.65°C). That was 0.20°C below November 2023 and 0.08°C below November 2024. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2025)
- **2026-10-12, latest bulletin:** September 2026 was the second-warmest September, at 16.27°C (+0.82°C, or 1.63°C above pre-industrial). That was 0.11°C below September 2023, but sea surface temperatures were a record for September. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-september-2026)
- **August 2026:** 16.96°C (+0.85°C), the warmest August and the joint-hottest month on record. [sustainabilityonline](https://sustainabilityonline.net/?p=34525)
- **C3S framing:** C3S said that if the last three months of 2026 match those of 2023, the 2026 annual average would be close to 2024's record. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-september-2026)

## 2. Current status
- **2026-10-30:** Nothing settles the question yet. The C3S November bulletin is expected in the first days or around 9 December. That would come after the stated resolve date of 2026-12-01.
- **2026-10-30:** celsius.earth (unofficial, based on ERA5 plus an ECMWF ensemble) estimates October 2026 month-to-date at +0.92°C. It calls the warmest October on record certain, 0.07°C above October 2023. [celsius.earth](https://celsius.earth/warmest-month)
  - An earlier search summary of the same page gave 45% for the October record, so its numbers have been updated over time.
- **2026-10-30:** The same site's November 2026 forecast is +0.83°C (90% range +0.66 to +1.01). That is 0.02°C below the November 2023 mark, which it treats as +0.85. It gives a **42%** chance of a record. [celsius.earth](https://celsius.earth/warmest-month)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- **2026-10-30:** ECMWF ensembles reportedly show an 86% chance of a major sudden stratospheric warming in early November. Business Today ties this to the El Niño. It could bring cold air to the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes, but its effect on the global mean is ambiguous. [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/world/story/arctic-polar-vortex-could-weaken-like-never-before-in-november-what-super-el-nino-has-to-do-with-it-564701-2026-10-30)
- **2026-10-29 / 10-28:** There are regional forecasts of an early-November cold spell in eastern Europe and an Omega block over France. These are regional and have little effect on the global mean. [Il Mattino](https://www.ilmattino.it/primopiano/cronaca/meteo_inverno_2026_2027_freddo_novembre_neve-9856429.html), [Futura](https://www.futura-sciences.com/planete/actualites/meteo-meteo-va-bloquer-france-pendant-10-15-jours-voici-cest-mauvaise-nouvelle-138904/)
- **2026-10-18:** The Niño 3.4 daily anomaly hit a record +3.35°C on 15 October, beating the 2015-16 mark of 3.08°C. The WMO expects an October-December mean of about +3.7°C, peaking around December. [Climate Adaptation Center](https://www.theclimateadaptationcenter.org/2026/10/18/el-nino-reaches-record-strength/)
- **October 2026:** NOAA puts the chance of the strongest El Niño on record at over 83%. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026%E2%80%932027_El_Ni%C3%B1o_event)
- **October 2026:** The Copernicus director suggested 2026 could be the hottest year on record. [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-10-el-nio-temperature-key-pacific.html)

## 4. Base rates
- **Recent November anomalies (ERA5, vs 1991-2020):** about +0.85 in 2023 (record), about +0.73 in 2024 and +0.65 in 2025. [C3S](https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2025)
- **Pattern:** New November records tend to come in strong El Niño years, such as 2015 and 2023. The global temperature response usually lags the El Niño peak by about 3 to 4 months, which favours early 2027 more than November.
- **2026 vs 2023, month by month:** August 2026 tied the record, September was 0.11°C short, and October looks set for a record by about 0.07°C.
- **What it takes:** Beating 0.85 requires November to hold roughly October's anomaly, at most dropping about 0.07°C.
- **Typical variation:** Month-to-month changes in the ERA5 global anomaly are often 0.05 to 0.15°C, so the margin here is within normal noise.

## 5. Other forecasts
- **2026-10-30, Kalshi "This November is the hottest November ever?":** Yes at **0.76**. It likely matches this question, but I did not verify which dataset it settles on.
- **Kalshi "November temperature increase?":** The "1.30 or above" bin is at 0.53. This is probably a NASA or NOAA-type metric, not ERA5, and I could not confirm its source.
- **Polymarket:** October 2026 1st hottest at 0.968. 2026 rank #1 among years at 0.895.
- **Kalshi:** 2026 hottest year at 0.80.
- **celsius.earth model:** 42% for a November record (see section 2).
- **Manifold:** There is a market on October's rank, but I found none on November. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/where-will-october-2026-rank-among)
- **Expert forecasts:** I found no expert forecast of the November ranking specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Early November:** C3S's October 2026 bulletin. It will confirm October's anomaly; a bigger margin over 2023 would support a November record.
- **Throughout November:** Daily ERA5 values on Copernicus Climate Pulse. The page did not show values when I fetched it. [Climate Pulse](https://pulse.climate.copernicus.eu/)
- **Early November:** The possible sudden stratospheric warming and Northern Hemisphere cold outbreaks.
- **Ongoing:** El Niño strengthening toward its December peak, and NOAA's ENSO update around 2026-11-12.
- **Early December:** The C3S November bulletin, which decides the question.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires**
About one month of weather remains, and C3S will publish its bulletin around 4 to 9 December 2026. For Yes, ERA5's global mean surface air temperature for November 2026 must reach at least 14.22°C, which is +0.85°C against 1991-2020. That is the November 2023 record, and a tie counts as Yes.

**(b) Status quo**
If October's estimated anomaly of about +0.92°C simply persisted, November would beat the record by about 0.07°C. The status quo therefore leans Yes.

**(c) Base rate**
- **2023 analog:** During the 2023 El Niño build-up, every month from June to December set a calendar-month record.
- **Persistence:** When the month before is already about 0.07°C above the target record and El Niño is still strengthening, the next month usually also sets a record. Month-to-month noise in the global anomaly is roughly ±0.08°C (one standard deviation).
- **Implied chance:** Starting from about +0.92 and needing at least +0.85, the chance is roughly 75-80%.

**(d) Strongest evidence**
For Yes:
- October 2026 is estimated at +0.92°C, a record by about 0.07°C (celsius.earth, ERA5 data through 29 October).
- The anomaly rose about 0.1°C from September (+0.82) to October.
- Niño 3.4 was at an all-time September high (C3S, October 2026), and global temperatures lag Niño 3.4 by a few months.
- Extra-polar sea surface temperatures are at records.
- Kalshi prices a November record at 0.76, though its resolution source may differ from C3S.

For No:
- The celsius.earth model's central November forecast is +0.83°C, just below the bar, giving a 42-59% chance of a record.
- The November 2023 bar is high: it was only a little below 2023's September and October values.
- A possible sudden stratospheric warming in early November (reported 30 October) adds variance.
- The October figure is a third-party estimate, not yet confirmed by C3S.

**(e) Scenarios**
- **No:** The stratospheric warming and blocking patterns cause short-term dips. The anomaly falls back to around +0.80 and November ends second, a few hundredths below 2023.
- **Yes:** El Niño-driven warmth keeps building, as it did from 2015 into 2016. November comes in around +0.90 to +0.95 and sets a record comfortably.

**(f) Adjustment**
- I start from the persistence base rate of about 78%.
- I shade down for the dissenting central estimate from the celsius.earth model and for the stratospheric-warming variance.
- I also shade down because Kalshi's 0.76 is not an exact match for the C3S resolution source.

This lands me at around 72%.

Probability: 72%

(a) About five weeks remain. C3S should publish the November bulletin around December 4 to 9, 2026. For Yes, the ERA5 global mean surface air temperature for November 2026 must be at least 14.22°C, or +0.85°C vs 1991-2020, matching or beating November 2023. A tie counts as Yes.

(b) Status quo: if the global anomaly simply persisted at October 2026's estimated +0.92°C, November would set a record. That points to Yes.

(c) Base rate: in strong El Niño build-up years, months that follow a calendar-month record usually set records too. In 2023, every month from June to December set one, and the 2015/16 pattern was similar. Conditional on the prior month being a record by about 0.07°C, the reference class gives roughly 75-80% Yes. The November bar is relatively high, though, because November 2023 was nearly as anomalous as October 2023.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - October 2026 is estimated at +0.92°C (celsius.earth, ERA5 data through 2026-10-29). That is about 0.07°C above the October record and above the +0.85 November bar.
  - Niño 3.4 set an all-time monthly high (C3S, September bulletin), and El Niño is still strengthening. Global temperatures lag Niño 3.4, which points to further warming.
  - Extra-polar sea surface temperatures are at record levels.
  - Kalshi prices a hottest November at 0.76, though its source is probably NASA, which correlates with ERA5.
- For No:
  - celsius.earth's November forecast is +0.83°C, with a 42-59% chance of a record (2026-10-30).
  - September 2026 was only second warmest, at +0.82 vs +0.93 in 2023.
  - A possible major sudden stratospheric warming in early November (ECMWF ensemble, 2026-10-30) could cause regional cold, though its effect on the global mean is ambiguous.
  - Month-to-month noise is about ±0.08°C.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: a weather-driven dip, such as a cold Antarctic or Northern Hemisphere land anomaly, pulls November to +0.80-0.84, just short of 2023.
- Yes: the El Niño-driven warming continues, November holds at +0.88-0.95, and C3S declares a record.

(f) My central estimate is around +0.90°C, between persistence (+0.92, with an upward El Niño drift) and the celsius model (+0.83). With a standard deviation of about 0.08, that gives roughly a 70-75% chance of exceeding +0.85. The Kalshi price of 0.76 is a moderate anchor, discounted for the possible source mismatch. The celsius.earth model pulls me down slightly, so I settle near 72%.

Probability: 72%

(a) About 5 weeks. C3S publishes the November bulletin around December 4-9, 2026. For Yes, the ERA5 global mean surface air temperature for November 2026 must be at least 14.22°C, an anomaly of about +0.85°C vs 1991-2020, which ties or beats November 2023.

(b) Status quo: global temperatures are running at record levels for the calendar month. October 2026 is estimated at about +0.92°C, roughly 0.07°C above the November bar. If November simply held October's anomaly, the answer would be Yes.

(c) Base rate: month-to-month changes in the global anomaly are typically about ±0.05-0.1°C. During strengthening El Niño episodes such as 2015-16 and 2023-24, the anomaly usually rises from October into the following winter. In the 2023 build-up, every month from June to December set a calendar-month record. Starting from +0.92°C with a +0.85°C bar, a persistence-plus-noise model gives roughly 75-85% Yes.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - October 2026 is estimated at about +0.92°C, a record by about 0.07°C (celsius.earth, 2026-10-30).
  - Niño 3.4 set an all-time September high (C3S, October 2026), and global temperatures lag Niño 3.4 by a few months.
  - The anomaly rose about 0.1°C from September (+0.82) to October.
  - Kalshi prices November as the hottest ever at 0.76, though its source may be NOAA or NASA rather than C3S.
- For No:
  - The celsius.earth model puts November at +0.83°C (42-59% chance of a record).
  - The bar is high: November 2023 was unusually warm relative to its season.
  - An 86% chance of a major sudden stratospheric warming in early November (Business Today, 2026-10-30) and Northern Hemisphere cold outbreaks could depress the global mean somewhat.

(e) No scenario: a sudden stratospheric warming and widespread cold over the Northern Hemisphere continents pull land temperatures down. November then comes in at about +0.80°C, second warmest behind 2023.
Yes scenario: El Niño warming of the tropical oceans keeps building, and November lands at about +0.90-0.98°C, a clear record.

(f) I start at about 80% from persistence. I trim slightly for the celsius.earth model's below-threshold central estimate and the stratospheric warming risk, and stay close to the Kalshi anchor of 0.76. That gives about 78%.

Probability: 78%

(a) The question resolves when C3S publishes the November 2026 ERA5 bulletin, expected in early December, about 5 to 6 weeks from now. Yes requires the November 2026 global surface air temperature anomaly to equal or exceed November 2023's, which is about +0.85°C above the 1991-2020 average (about 14.22°C).

(b) Status quo: if October's anomaly (about +0.92°C month-to-date, a record) simply persists into November, the result is Yes by about 0.07°C. Persistence of the current state favours Yes, but only modestly, because the margin is within normal month-to-month noise.

(c) Base rate: in strong El Niño years with the global anomaly already at record levels in October (2015, 2023), November set or matched a record in both cases. In 2023, October and November had similar anomalies, about +0.85 each. Month-to-month changes of 0.05 to 0.15°C make a 0.07°C cushion roughly a 65 to 75% proposition on persistence alone. Taking the October record as given, my base rate is about 65%.

(d) Evidence:
